newsitem.title: INDIA: EU envoys hear conflicting views in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: EU envoys hear conflicting views in Kashmir.

text.p: Kashmiri separatists and Indian authorities have given the Europe Union sharply contrasting assessments of the ground situation in the Himalayan region, officials said on Wednesday.
A five-member EU delegation met officials of Jammu and Kashmir state, including army and police, late on Tuesday in the state's summer capital Srinagar.
"The authorities apprised the envoys about the fast-improving situation and security scenario in the (Kashmir) valley," a state government spokesman said.
The envoys met representatives of the leading separatist alliance on Wednesday.

"We educated these envoys about the deteriorating situation in the valley after elections and gave them a first-hand report about the political and human rights situation," Umar Farooq, chairman of the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, told Reuters.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year separatist rebellion in the Himalayan region.
The state's chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, has said some 50,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence.
The Hurriyat is comprised of nearly 30 separatist groups opposed to mostly Hindu India's rule over the Moslem-majority Kashmir Valley.
Indian authorities say militancy is on the wane, as evidenced by the holding last year of the first state assembly elections since the outbreak of the revolt.
But separatist leaders accuse government security forces of repressive tactics in combating the movement.
The EU delegation was comprised of the ambassadors of Ireland, Italy and the Netherlands to India, a British diplomat and the head of the European Commission's delegation in New Delhi.
During Tuesday's meetings, state government officials appealed to the EU for financial aid and technical expertise.
The delegation was to meet Abdullah, human rights activists and Shabir Shah, a popular Kashmiri separatist leader, during its three-day visit to the Kashmir Valley.
